about: Plain readings for the hand check, one per drawn game and predicate, used by scripts/handcheck_app.py to write docs/truth/handcheck_rows.json. deciding: the line to highlight, in the description ('description', line) or the row's own level file ('level'). In a reading, {n} is replaced by the count the generator read from that row's level file. These readings explain the generator's verdict; they are not answers.

clusters/A1.reading: The sprite placed by A is a MovingAvatar: it steps up, down, left or right, one key for each.
clusters/A1.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong only if a MovingAvatar answered to fewer than two different keys, which in GVGAI is true only of NullAvatar and MissileAvatar.

clusters/A2.reading: When the avatar walks into a box, the box is pushed one square forward, so the arrow keys move boxes as well as the avatar.
clusters/A2.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if a box pushed by the avatar did not count as a second sprite moved by the player's action.

clusters/A3.reading: The avatar is a MovingAvatar with no speed given, so speed 1, and no line of the InteractionSet carries the avatar anywhere; stepBack only cancels its step.
clusters/A3.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if some interaction with the avatar first moved it, as wrapAround or bounceForward would.

clusters/A4.reading: Walls (line 37) and the coloured blocks (line 49) send the avatar back, and both are Immovable (lines 7 and 19).
clusters/A4.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if blocks appeared without the player: line 42 turns a box into a block when the box reaches a block, and the generator counts that as the avatar's doing because only the avatar pushes boxes.

clusters/A5.reading: The game is won when no box is left (line 61 of the description), and this level places {n} boxes, not one.
clusters/A5.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if the level held a single box, or if the winning line counted something other than boxes.

colourescape/A1.reading: normalAvatar, placed by A, sits under line 19, avatar > MovingAvatar, so it is a MovingAvatar.
colourescape/A1.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if normalAvatar did not take the class MovingAvatar from its parent line 19.

colourescape/A2.reading: When normalAvatar walks into a plain box the box is pushed forward; lines 47, 50 and 53 do the same for the coloured boxes and avatars.
colourescape/A2.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if a pushed box did not count as a second sprite moved by the player's action.

colourescape/A3.reading: All four avatar kinds are MovingAvatar at speed 1; a switch (lines 64 to 67) changes the avatar's colour, not its place.
colourescape/A3.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if changing the avatar's kind with transformTo counted as an interaction that moves it.

colourescape/A4.reading: Walls send the avatar back, and walls are Immovable (line 25).
colourescape/A4.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if the moves cancelled at lines 48, 51, 54 and 57 (an avatar of the wrong colour pushing a box, undoAll) needed a blocker that moves on its own; there the boxes come first in the line and move only when an avatar pushes them.

colourescape/A5.reading: The game is won when no exit is left, the level places {n} exit, and only the avatar removes it (line 61).
colourescape/A5.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if some sprite other than the avatar could remove the exit, or if there were a second winning line.

glow/A1.reading: The avatar is a ShootAvatar: it moves with the arrow keys and fires with the use key.
glow/A1.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong only if a ShootAvatar answered to fewer than two different keys.

glow/A2.reading: A ShootAvatar's use key creates a new sprite, here a spark (stype=spark), so the action makes a second object as well as moving the avatar.
glow/A2.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if the use key created nothing, for instance if stype named no sprite.

glow/A3.reading: The line does not set rotateInPlace=False, and a ShootAvatar by default turns to face a new direction on the first press instead of stepping.
glow/A3.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if this line or a parent line set rotateInPlace=False.

glow/A4.reading: Walls and the edge of the screen (EOS) send the avatar back, and walls are Immovable (line 18).
glow/A4.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if something else stopped the avatar, or if walls could be made or removed during play; the bridges and traps of lines 31 to 34 change or kill sprites but do not block.

glow/A5.reading: There are two ways to win: no exit left (line 39) and lasting until the time limit (line 40, Timeout win=True), so reaching the goal is not the only win.
glow/A5.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if the Timeout line with win=True did not count as a winning condition.

labyrinthdual/A1.reading: avatarNormal, placed by A, sits under line 15, avatar > MovingAvatar, so it is a MovingAvatar.
labyrinthdual/A1.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if avatarNormal did not take the class MovingAvatar from its parent line 15.

labyrinthdual/A2.reading: The only avatar at start is avatarNormal, a MovingAvatar whose use key creates nothing, and no line pushes or pulls a sprite the avatar walks into.
labyrinthdual/A2.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if the level placed more than one avatar, or if picking up a coat (lines 28 and 31, which remove the coat) counted as the action moving another sprite.

labyrinthdual/A3.reading: All three avatar kinds are MovingAvatar at speed 1; putting on a coat (lines 28 and 31) changes the avatar's kind, not its place.
labyrinthdual/A3.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if changing the avatar's kind with transformTo counted as an interaction that moves it.

labyrinthdual/A4.reading: Walls send the avatar back (lines 22 to 25), each colour of wall for some avatar kinds only, and all walls are Immovable (line 7).
labyrinthdual/A4.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if a set of blockers that changes with the coat the player puts on (lines 24 and 25) did not count as fixed by the player's own actions.

labyrinthdual/A5.reading: The game is won when no exit is left, the level places {n} exit, and only the avatar removes it (line 33).
labyrinthdual/A5.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if some sprite other than the avatar could remove the exit, or if there were a second winning line.

lasers/A1.reading: The avatar is a ShootAvatar: it moves with the arrow keys and fires with the use key.
lasers/A1.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong only if a ShootAvatar answered to fewer than two different keys.

lasers/A2.reading: The use key fires a boulder (stype=boulder), and line 37 pushes a box when the avatar walks into it: two ways the action moves something besides the avatar.
lasers/A2.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if neither the shot boulder nor the pushed box counted as a second sprite moved by the action.

lasers/A3.reading: The avatar is a ShootAvatar with rotateInPlace=true, so pressing a new direction first turns it without moving it.
lasers/A3.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if rotateInPlace=true did not make the first press in a new direction a turn.

lasers/A4.reading: Walls and laser cannons send the avatar back; walls are Immovable, cannons are SpawnPoint (line 7) and never move, and a cannon changes kind only when the avatar's boulder hits it (lines 49 to 53).
lasers/A4.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if a SpawnPoint did not count as staying in place, or if the boulder the avatar fires did not count as the avatar's own action.

lasers/A5.reading: The game is won when no goal is left, the level places {n} goal, and only the avatar removes it (line 47).
lasers/A5.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if some sprite other than the avatar could remove the goal, or if there were a second winning line.

painter/A1.reading: The avatar is a MovingAvatar: it steps up, down, left or right, one key for each.
painter/A1.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong only if a MovingAvatar answered to fewer than two different keys.

painter/A2.reading: The one avatar is a MovingAvatar whose use key creates nothing, and no line pushes or pulls a sprite the avatar walks into.
painter/A2.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if a sprite made by walking counted as a second sprite moved by the action: line 29 spawns prepaint wherever the avatar steps on ground.

painter/A3.reading: The avatar is a MovingAvatar at speed 1, and no line carries it anywhere; the edge only sends it back (line 26).
painter/A3.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if some interaction with the avatar first moved it.

painter/A4.reading: Only the edge of the screen sends the avatar back (avatar EOS > stepBack); no sprite blocks it, not even wall, which has no interaction line.
painter/A4.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if some move had no effect for a reason other than the edge.

painter/A5.reading: The game is won when no ground is left (line 41 of the description), and this level places {n} ground tiles, not one.
painter/A5.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if the level held a single ground tile, or if the winning line counted something other than ground.

racebet/A1.reading: normal, placed by A, sits under line 25, avatar > MovingAvatar speed=1.0, so it is a MovingAvatar.
racebet/A1.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if normal did not take the class MovingAvatar from its parent line 25.

racebet/A2.reading: The only avatar at start is normal, a MovingAvatar that creates nothing; stepping on a pit (lines 37 to 41) changes its kind and moves nothing else.
racebet/A2.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if the level placed more than one avatar, or if the camels, which run on their own (line 6), moved because of the player's keys.

racebet/A3.reading: Every avatar kind takes MovingAvatar speed=1.0 from line 25, and no line carries the avatar anywhere.
racebet/A3.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if speed=1.0 were not speed 1, or if changing the avatar's kind on a pit counted as moving it.

racebet/A4.reading: Only walls send the avatar back, and walls are Immovable (line 33); the camels run on their own but never block the avatar.
racebet/A4.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if a camel or a barrier could stop the avatar; line 49 stops only camels.

racebet/A5.reading: The winning lines (68 to 71) are MultiSpriteCounter lines that count a winning camel and a bet together, not a single SpriteCounter with limit 0, so there is no single goal to reach.
racebet/A5.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if a MultiSpriteCounter with limit 2 counted as a single place goal under the registered wording.

rivers/A1.reading: The avatar is a ShootAvatar: it moves with the arrow keys and uses its shovel with the use key.
rivers/A1.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong only if a ShootAvatar answered to fewer than two different keys.

rivers/A2.reading: The use key creates a shovel sprite (stype=shovel), a second object made by the action.
rivers/A2.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if the use key created nothing, for instance if stype named no sprite.

rivers/A3.reading: The line does not set rotateInPlace=False, and a ShootAvatar by default turns to face a new direction on the first press instead of stepping.
rivers/A3.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if this line or a parent line set rotateInPlace=False.

rivers/A4.reading: Houses send the avatar back (line 32), and this line turns a dry house into a wet one when water reaches it; water is not the avatar, so a blocker is replaced without the player's own step.
rivers/A4.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if water counted as driven by the avatar (it flows only into holes the shovel digs, lines 36 and 40), or if swapping one blocking house for another in the same square did not count as changing the blockers.

rivers/A5.reading: The game is won when no dry house is left (line 45 of the description), and this level places {n} dry houses, not one.
rivers/A5.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if the level held a single dry house, or if the winning line counted something other than dry houses.

sokoban/A1.reading: The avatar is a MovingAvatar: it steps up, down, left or right, one key for each.
sokoban/A1.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong only if a MovingAvatar answered to fewer than two different keys.

sokoban/A2.reading: When the avatar walks into a box, the box is pushed one square forward, so the arrow keys move boxes as well as the avatar.
sokoban/A2.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if a box pushed by the avatar did not count as a second sprite moved by the player's action.

sokoban/A3.reading: The avatar is a MovingAvatar with no speed given, so speed 1, and no line carries it anywhere; stepBack only cancels its step.
sokoban/A3.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if some interaction with the avatar first moved it.

sokoban/A4.reading: Walls send the avatar back and are Immovable (line 7); a box pushed into a wall also cancels the avatar's step (line 17), and boxes move only when the avatar pushes them.
sokoban/A4.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if a box, which can stop the avatar through undoAll at line 17, moved or vanished other than through the avatar's push; it falls into a hole (line 18) only after a push.

sokoban/A5.reading: The game is won when no box is left (line 20 of the description), and this level places {n} boxes, not one.
sokoban/A5.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if the level held a single box, or if the winning line counted something other than boxes.

wrapsokoban/A1.reading: The avatar is an OrientedAvatar: it moves with the four arrow keys.
wrapsokoban/A1.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong only if an OrientedAvatar answered to fewer than two different keys.

wrapsokoban/A2.reading: When the avatar walks into a box, the box is pushed one square forward, so the arrow keys move boxes as well as the avatar.
wrapsokoban/A2.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if a box pushed by the avatar did not count as a second sprite moved by the player's action.

wrapsokoban/A3.reading: When the avatar walks off the edge of the screen it reappears on the other side, so at the edge one step does not move it by one square.
wrapsokoban/A3.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if the level's walls kept the avatar from ever reaching the edge, so that the wrap could never happen.

wrapsokoban/A4.reading: Walls send the avatar back and are Immovable (line 11).
wrapsokoban/A4.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if a box, which can stop the avatar through undoAll at line 25, moved or changed other than through the avatar's push.

wrapsokoban/A5.reading: The game is won when no box is left (line 30 of the description), and this level places {n} boxes, not one.
wrapsokoban/A5.wrong_if: The verdict would be wrong if the level held a single box, or if the winning line counted something other than boxes.
